correctness.rationale: Derivative R prime is strictly negative, so G(s)=log(1-exp(-exp(s))) is increasing strictly concave. Both log-input functions are strictly concave; therefore log F is strictly concave. Endpoint limits guarantee unique global optimum and positive derivative through 1/b. Derivative sign at 2/b yields exactly C versus Ae^-2. The asymptotic proof uses the exact stationarity relation and a logarithmic inequality; all parameters and equality cases covered. Standalone checker passed 24,077 supplementary numerical assertions.

value.rationale: For the ecologically motivated objective of confirming two targets with the same sample input, the theorem proves the inhibited-target-alone optimum is always suboptimal and gives a sharp twofold-input boundary C=Ae^-2. The threshold compares abundance/sensitivity parameters rather than an unmotivated slice, and provides an interpretable benchmark for inhibition-sensitive multi-target assay designs. Field calibration is explicitly excluded.
